slotAccounting.namingDeviation: The brief suggested HUMAN_APPROVED; this ships `human-required` because the engine has NO approval signal and must not claim a human approved anything. 'REVIEWED' was avoided as instructed — editability='review' already means something else.

syntheticProvenance: Two ways in, one way out. (1) The generator may declare keys in the new optional ContentGenerationResult.synthetic[]. (2) The engine's own deterministic detector (src/content-injection/truth-mode.ts:35 FACT_CLAIM_PATTERNS) matches observable claim SHAPES in the produced value: counted-metric, price, percentage, phone-number, certification-or-award, superlative-social-proof, founding-date. A match that is not backed — sources[key] !== 'user-provided', no providedFacts entry contained in the value, and the value is not byte-identical to the source default — is refused under verified-only (moved to `unresolved` with reason 'needs factual input: unsupported <claim> claim (content truth mode: verified-only)') and kept-and-marked under synthetic-allowed. Marked values land in slot-accounting.json as origin 'synthetic-fact', and every decision is listed in the artifact's truthDecisions[] as refused-unresolved | marked-synthetic | backed-by-user-fact. generated-marketing and derived-copy stay separate origins and are never re-labelled.

limitations: THE FACT DETECTOR MATCHES SHAPES, NOT TRUTH. It catches a counted metric, a price, a percentage, a phone number, a certification, a superlative social proof and a founding date. A fabricated claim expressed without any of those shapes ('our founder previously ran a national bank') passes straight through as generated-marketing. verified-only is therefore a strong guard against the common fabrications, NOT a proof of truthfulness, and the handoff must not be read as one.

THE SAME DETECTOR CAN OVER-TRIGGER. '24/7 support' matches percentage/metric shapes in some phrasings and would be withheld under verified-only. That is the conservative direction by design, but an operator will occasionally have to add a providedFacts entry for copy that is not really a claim.

THE TRUTH MODE IS ENFORCED AT INGEST ONLY. revalidateSlotValues (the §29 manual-edit path) does NOT re-run it: a value the operator typed by hand is theirs, and the accounting records it as user-provided. An operator can therefore hand-write a claim the mode would have refused.

GED-D IS WIRED INTO THE CLI REPAIR LOOP (src/cli-content-qa.ts) ONLY. Nothing else in the repo runs a repair loop today, so the release orchestrator never exercises the guard. The guard itself is a pure, exported class and is unit-tested independently of the CLI.

THE PROVIDER HALF OF GED-D IS NOT DONE, BY INSTRUCTION. providers.ts:83 `Math.max(4, target)` still produces a value shorter slots cannot use; the loop now stops instead of looping, but the micro-slot is still not repaired. It ends up in the operator report, which is the honest outcome.

BATCH EXECUTION IS ON THE PROVIDER PATH ONLY. The manual --result seam is one out-of-process file by design, so its telemetry event covers the whole packet and its batchIds list every batch rather than one.
NO REAL PROVIDER EXISTS, SO THE TELEMETRY USAGE FIELDS HAVE NEVER BEEN POPULATED BY A REAL SDK. They are exercised only by a stub in the smoke suite. Every real run in this repo leaves them absent.
REGIONPLAN HAS NO CONSUMER BEYOND ITS ARTIFACT. Nothing generates per-region, nothing batches per-region, nothing renders from it. It is the layer the hierarchy was missing, not yet a behaviour.

REGION GRANULARITY IS NOT UNIFORM and the PageRegion handoff says so: a page authored entirely in <div>s yields few, large regions. linear's homepage gave 12 plans with 0 unassigned units, but `unassignedUnitIds` is expected to be non-empty on such a template and is reported rather than papered over.

THE ACCOUNTING DENOMINATOR IS THE TEMPLATE'S IN-SCOPE SLOT SET, NOT 'every customer-facing thing on the page'. templateExcludedCandidates (1,435 on linear) counts candidates the Slot V2 compiler suppressed before slotting; they are named in the artifact but cannot be accounted for, because the engine never saw them.

TWO PREPARES AT THE SAME runId ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL, BUT A REPREPARE AFTER A TEMPLATE RECOMPILE IS NOT GUARANTEED TO BE: batch ids follow unit ids, which follow slots.json order. That was already true before Task 27; nothing here made it worse and nothing here fixed it.

THE TRUTH MODE HAS NEVER BEEN TRIPPED BY A REAL RUN. Its enforcement path is exercised positively ONLY by constructed fixtures in the smoke suite. The real linear.app exercise recorded truthDecisions = [] and 0 slots of origin `synthetic-fact`, because FakeContentGenerator emits 'Fake na…' strings that match none of the seven claim shapes. The mode is proven not-ignored end to end (a run persists its mode, and a constructed claim is demoted through the real ingest path), but no end-to-end run against real template data has ever produced a value that tripped it. Only a real provider will exercise that.

THREE NEW ContentRunManifest FIELDS ARE WRITTEN AND NEVER READ: `batching`, `repairStop` and `slotAccounting`. No code in the repo consumes them today — they are an audit trail for an operator or a later stage, not wired-up behaviour. Do not mistake their presence for a consumer. (`slotAccounting` and `truthMode` are offered to src/release in the changeRequests above, which is 2B's call.)

The suite itself is fine — the second run passed 130/130 — but a single red run of it on a multi-agent tree is not by itself evidence of a defect.

truthModeDefaultDecision.question: Is `verified-only` the right DEFAULT, given it can DEMOTE a value a Task 19 run already applied?
truthModeDefaultDecision.whatActuallyChanged: A real, stricter ENGINE behaviour — NOT a no-op, and the earlier framing of it as 'the behaviour every Task 19 run already had' was WRONG. Task 19's no-invented-facts rule bound only the PROMPT (src/content-injection/truth-mode.ts:15-18 says so in its own words). With this module in the ingest path, re-ingesting a HISTORICAL generation result whose copy matches one of the seven claim shapes (percentage /\b\d[\d.]*\s?%/, price, superlative-social-proof 'trusted by', counted metric, phone number, certification, founding date — truth-mode.ts:65-82) now moves that value out of `slotValues` and into `unresolved`.
truthModeDefaultDecision.whoItCanAffect: Anyone re-running `content:generate --result <archived.json>`, and any release rerun that re-ingests an archived result: a slot that used to be applied becomes an operator ask, so a project that read PRODUCTION_READY can read INPUTS_REQUIRED after a rerun. No artifact already on disk changes until it is re-ingested; nothing was rewritten by this wave.
reasoning: The demotion is LOUD, not silent. It is printed by content:generate (src/cli-content-generate.ts:143-153 prints the mode, the counts and every withheld slot key with its claim shape and the exact flag that keeps it), recorded per slot in slot-accounting.json truthDecisions[], and surfaced as a needs-input slot in the operator review. The failure mode of the other default — shipping an unbacked 'Trusted by 4,000 teams' on a customer's production site — is silent.

The escape hatch is LOSSLESS, so preserving history costs exactly one flag and loses nothing: under `--truth-mode synthetic-allowed` every value is kept verbatim and the resulting overlay is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what Task 19 produced; the only difference is that the invention is now recorded (origin `synthetic-fact`). This is measured, not asserted — the smoke compares the ingested overlay against buildOverlayValues(historicalResult) with JSON.stringify.
Defaulting to `synthetic-allowed` would leave `no-invented-facts` a prompt request forever, which is the exact Task 19 gap §4 was opened to close.
truthModeDefaultDecision.legibleInTheSuite: scripts/smoke-content-injection.ts §4 — two new checks pin a Task-19-shaped historical result (a 'trusted by' hero and a '$19 a month, 99.9% uptime since 2019' footer): (1) 're-ingesting a HISTORICAL Task-19 result DEMOTES its fact-shaped values (a real behaviour change, not a no-op)' — both values leave the overlay, exactly 2 refused-unresolved decisions, both entries disposition `unresolved`; (2) 'the escape hatch is LOSSLESS: synthetic-allowed reproduces the Task 19 overlay byte-for-byte' — overlay JSON equals buildOverlayValues(historical) and both entries carry origin `synthetic-fact`.

hardening.what: '§7 every recorded field is observed, never fabricated' only typeof-checked fields the zod schema already guarantees. It is replaced by '§7 a provider with no usage hook leaves `usage` off EVERY line — never zero-filled, never estimated', which parses the RAW JSONL lines and asserts no line carries a `usage` key when the generator implements no lastUsage() hook. A zero-filled or token-estimating recorder fails it; the previous check could not fail.
hardening.note: This is strictly stronger than the neighbouring manual-seam check, which inspects only the LAST line; the new one covers every batch-call line too.

hardening.what: src/content-injection/repair.ts noRepairCandidatesStop(completedIterations) now writes 'never started: the first layout QA report produced no repairable slot …' when 0 iterations completed, and 'stopped after N completed iteration(s): no repairable slot remained …' otherwise. Both `no-repair-candidates` call sites in src/cli-content-qa.ts (:178 and :267) route through it. Pinned by 'GED-D `no-repair-candidates` distinguishes NEVER STARTED from stopped-after-N'.

hardening.item: 5 — three manifest fields are written but never read
hardening.what: ContentRunManifest.batching, .repairStop and .slotAccounting are written by this wave and read by no code in the repo. They are an audit trail, not wired-up behaviour, and the limitation now says so.
